entry.title: What Are You Making? That’s Deadly!

media:group.media:title: What Are You Making? That’s Deadly!
media:group.media:description:
Nicholas Currie is an artist and curator working with painting, sculpture and performance. Currie is from the Mununjali clan of the Yugambeh language group, with connection to Kuku Yalanji, and currently lives on Wurundjeri Country in Naarm/Melbourne. Humour and kindness are undercurrents to the major themes addressed in his works: contemporary Indigenous perspectives, hauntology and exploration of identity within current Australia.
MUMA x MITS Education Partnership
Since 2017, MUMA and Melbourne Indigenous Transition School (MITS) have built an enduring partnership connecting First Nations students with First Nations artists. Through sustained, artist-led engagement, students learn directly from artists, share knowledge, build confidence and explore creative practice. This work strengthens relationships while centering First Nations perspectives, culture, experience, knowledge and creativity.
What Are You Making? That’s Deadly!
In 2026, MUMA invited Nicholas Currie to present the workshop ‘What Are You Making? That’s Deadly!’ for the Year 7 MITS students. The young artists were encouraged to sculpt, paint, engrave and glaze, together creating an installation of ceramic footballs holding stories of Country and culture.

media:group.media:title: Philip Meng - Master of TESOL
media:group.media:description: Philip Meng, a Monash University TESOL alumnus, is now an English teacher at an international high school in Shanghai. Drawn to Monash by its strong global reputation and recommendations from family, he found more than just academic excellence during his time in Melbourne. From memorable experiences outside the classroom, including forming a band, to developing innovative teaching approaches and practical classroom skills, his Monash journey helped shape the educator he is today. Discover how he continues to inspire and empower students, helping them realise their potential and create positive change through learning.

entry.title: Monash's Global Immersion Guarantee (GIG) - Country Highlights

media:group.media:title: Monash's Global Immersion Guarantee (GIG) - Country Highlights
media:group.media:description:
The Global Immersion Guarantee (GIG) is your chance to learn from local leaders about how they’re working to address the human impact on the environment. See first-hand how to balance environmental protection and sustainability with economic and social development - and discover how you can contribute and make a difference.
GIG is a funded 12-credit point fieldwork unit (MON2100) that takes you to one of eight countries at the end of your first year.
You could travel to one of the following countries: - India - Indonesia - Fiji - Samoa - Vanuatu - Malaysia - Italy - China - Vietnam
Take this unique opportunity to put your degree into practice and respond to some of the world’s biggest challenges. You'll gain a deeper understanding of the complexities and challenges involved in implementing sustainable and innovative solutions - skills that employers hold in high esteem.
Flights, accommodation, visas and all program costs are paid for while you’re abroad - you just need to cover the tuition fees, some food and spending money!
Apply now: https://www.monash.edu/flagship-rich-experiences/gig
